plant.verbatim: caps are still grey and read as cement, not stone

seat.BEST_WHY: The floor slabs in the lit zone (roughly x 180–420, y 450–620) are actually built rather than tiled. The joints are a 1px stipple whose interruptions differ slab to slab, so no two seams read the same length; the slab interiors carry three distinct tooling treatments — short vertical chisel ticks, a fine 45° hatch, and blank stone — distributed without pattern; and slab widths vary, with double-width blocks breaking the course. Most tellingly, the hairline crack entering at the lower left runs continuously across four separate slabs and over their joints, ignoring the tile boundary entirely. Cracks that respect the grid are stamped; this one was drawn over the finished surface. The wall runs at y≈388–420 also carry thin vertical pins at x≈350 and x≈700 driven through the timber — the only thing in the deck that matches the repair vocabulary of the place.
seat.WORST_WHY: The water body is a rectangle. Its left edge sits at exactly x=248 and its right edge at exactly x=343 on row 40, row 100 and row 160 — identical to the pixel, three times down the frame — and it terminates in a flat horizontal cut at y≈190. There is no shoreline, no edge tile, no single pixel of transition between teal water and brown dirt anywhere on its perimeter. The dirt field around it is worse: of 432 16px blocks in the frame only 193 are unique, and one dirt block from (160,0) recurs verbatim 15 times on a regular 48px lattice — (112,48), (160,48), (208,48), (64,96), (112,96) — so the entire mud area is one 3×3 patch stamped edge to edge, with the seam visible. The dirt-to-stone boundary is likewise raw square steps with no transition. On top of that: the frame has zero light falloff, uniformly bright corner to corner, in a game whose premise is that the figure carries the only light; the green figure at top-centre is drawn at a different outline weight and saturation from everything else and is the only object in the frame carrying a soft elliptical drop shadow (the two barrels at y≈200 cast none); the lily pads are primary saturated green against an otherwise fully desaturated brown/grey scene; and the bone scatter at ~(215,115) is white noise with no readable form.

flip_list: A uniform ~45° hatch overlay runs across the entire lit floor at one pitch and one angle, crossing stones, crossing joints, and continuing into the dark zone unchanged. It is screen-space, not surface texture, and it is the single thing that makes the frame read as filtered. Remove it; put the hatch into individual stones as tooling, varying angle per stone as image 3 does.
The region x 130–440, y 0–140 is soft brown blobs with no joints and no edges — stones dissolved by blur. Redraw it with hard 1px joints at the tile pitch.

The wall top surface immediately right of the figure at (490,470) measures luminance 170 against the floor below it at (520,500) measuring 68. The wall is 2.5× brighter than the floor it stands on and reads as a white smear rather than a solid. Cap wall-top luminance below adjacent lit floor.

There is a vertical column of light at x≈510–530 running y 250–450, measuring 70 against 54 immediately beside it, with nothing in the frame casting it. In a straight top-down view there is no geometry that produces a vertical shaft. Delete it.
In the lit zone right of the figure the stone joints vanish entirely — you cannot tell where one slab ends. Restore joint contrast at full light so the grid survives exposure.
Overall: the frame is soft everywhere. Kill the blur pass and let the tiles land on the pixel grid.
law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.
